correctness.rationale: The reproducible Python verifier enumerates all 115975 faces and all 597155 Hasse incidences, checks the complete acyclic matching by directed topological sort, constructs the signed exact integral Morse boundary matrices and checks consecutive compositions vanish. Unit Smith elimination gives ranks 694,219,1 and zero residual blocks; hence every nonzero invariant factor equals 1. Reduced groups are Z^402 in degree four, Z^815 in degree five, and zero otherwise. St(8) recomputes published 24,292,1 as a separate reference control. The proof is finite for nine rows only.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2010 Clark–Zeckner paper explicitly asks whether the nine-row staircase Stirling rook complex has torsion and publishes numerical homology only through eight rows. An exact computation of the full nine-row integral groups, including both free ranks and absence of torsion, is not implied by that table or the earlier connectivity theorem. Searches of indexed published claims, object aliases and exact ranks revealed no directly covering result. Publication priority remains subject to the inaccessible 2011 Zeckner dissertation and any unindexed literature.

value.rationale: The nine-row staircase Stirling rook complex was explicitly singled out in the primary 2010 paper as the first case beyond its numerical table, with a concrete open question about torsion. Exact integral homology resolves that natural question and both missing Betti ranks, using genuine unimodular computations rather than numerical field checks. No infinite-family or homotopy decomposition is asserted.
